query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Designing a microstructure with optimized lamellar colony size and orientation will improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries
generation.intervention: Microstructure optimization through controlled solidification and thermomechanical processing to achieve a refined lamellar colony size of 10-50 μm and a preferred orientation of the lamellae
generation.structural_mediator: Refined lamellar colony size and optimized orientation
generation.mechanism: Reduced microcracking and improved strain accommodation through optimized lamellar colony size and orientation, leading to enhanced strength and ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in yield strength and 30% increase in tensile elongation compared to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline
generation.baseline: Unmodified dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries
generation.boundary: Lamellar colony size between 10-50 μm and orientation deviation within 10°
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in strength and ductility may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of optimized and unmodified eutectic high-entropy alloy samples at room temperature
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized samples exhibit less than 10% increase in yield strength or less than 20% increase in tensile elongation compared to the unmodified samples, the hypothesis is falsified
